correctness.rationale: The edge form in the frozen proof is the GHM form of Gravner–Lyu–Sivakoff Theorem 3. The hub triangles generate the cycle space and give circulation 0 unless tricolored, then ±1. Zero circulation on each triangle implies synchronization and all-rest. A nonzero triangle gives excitation frequency at least 1/3 at every vertex, and the refractory step imposes at least three steps per excitation. On the finite periodic tail this forces every gap to equal three, hence primitive period three. With hub phase zero, the rim condition must be tested over all three phases: initially 0 needs an adjacent 1, initially 1 needs an adjacent 2 at the later resting step, and initially 2 is forced through its resting step by the hub. The trace counts labelled closed rim strings, the one all-2 string must be removed, and fixing the hub phase counts each orbit once. Exact independent determinant calculation gives t⁴(t²+t+1)(t³−2t²−1). Newton sums yield the stated recurrence and root-of-unity term. The extinction matrix forbids 12 and 21 for hub 0; its eigenvalues are 1 and 1±sqrt(2), and the same trace applies for each hub color. The cubic has only one real root, λ>2 (both stationary values are negative); the complex roots have modulus λ^(−1/2), so the leading powers and both probability scales follow. Independent enumeration for n=3,…,10 gives exactly one fixed orbit and 12,22,50,116,252,558,1236,2722 three-cycles, with extinction sizes 45,105,249,597,1437,3465,8361,20181.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration is corroboration only. At RESULT.md lines 41–45 the test is a three-phase orbit-consistency test, not a replacement for the one-step GHM rule. No other update rule or transient bound is verified by the frozen proof.
